#178. Inside 'Grand Theft Auto VI'—and the Real-Life Florida Locations That Inspired It

📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10 min read (1968 words)
General 🌐 Cntraveler

Inside 'Grand Theft Auto VI'—and the Real-Life Florida Locations That Inspired It

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read | Source: Cntraveler

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that set to be released on November 19, 2026, Grand Theft Auto VI is expected to be the most profitable piece of media ever created.
  • Dreamt up by Scottish developers Rockstar Games, the GTA series has been big business for some time now.
  • According to recent reports, if you haven’t played the games, you should know that they take place in a sort of shadow version of the US, with each game taking place in a latest city inspired by a real-world counterpart.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that set to be released on November 19, 2026, Grand Theft Auto VI is expected to be the most profitable piece of media ever created. Pre-sale estimates suggest the game has made a staggering $476 million in revenue already.

Dreamt up by Scottish developers Rockstar Games, the GTA series has been big business for some time now. The previous instalment, Grand Theft Auto V has reportedly made a whopping $11 billion since its release in 2013. Not bad for a game in which you essentially steal cars and shoot guns.

According to recent reports, if you haven’t played the games, you should know that they take place in a sort of shadow version of the US, with each game taking place in a latest city inspired by a real-world counterpart. For me, they’ve been a fascinating companion to my travels in America. When I’m in New York, walking among towering skyscrapers, I can’t help but be reminded of Liberty City, the location of 2001’s dark and atmospheric Grand Theft Auto III. On holiday in Los Angeles, driving along the Pacific Coast Highway, the long, ocean-view roads of GTA V’s Los Santos were front of mind.

It works both ways. Red Dead Redemption 2, an open-world cowboy game released by Rockstar between GTAs V and VI, is perhaps the most immersive video game to date. In it, you can wander everywhere from dry, open deserts to lush forests where you can kick back with your horse, camp, and look for rare herbs and flowers. For me, it’s inspired trips to the deserts of the American Southwest and served as an interesting entry point into learning about US history. Now when I’m abroad, I’m thinking of these games, but also learning more about the real-world events and cultures that inspired them. It’s a full-circle moment that only enriches my travels.

These gaming vacations, or ‘gami-vacations’, are becoming increasingly popular. Fans are traveling to Tokyo to visit real-life locations from the Yakuza series and role-playing classic Persona 5, to Paris to see locations featured in the Assassin’s Creed series, to the Pacific Northwest to soak up the vibes of zombie classic Day Gone, and to Iceland to walk dramatic black sand beaches like those in the Hellblade series.

It has been revealed that “Santa Monica, the Sunset Strip, and Griffith Observatory from GTA V,” one Reddit user replied to a post asking about video game locations fans wanted to visit in real life. “Old town Tallinn feels like a very fairytale environment to me. If you went in winter, it would feel like a set from Assassin's Creed,” suggests another Redditor.

Sources indicate that far from being confined to their rooms, crouched over consoles, gamers are increasingly inspired to get out into the world. It’s a beautiful tradition, and one that GTA 6 looks set to continue. Set in the fictional state of Leonida, GTA 6 is set to be the franchise’s largest map to date. With six key locations, there promises to be something for every type of traveller. Here’s what you need to know, along with the real-world inspirations for each game location.

“We’re a long way from the ‘80s, but Vice City is still the sun and fun capital of America,” reads Rockstar’s official guide to GTA VI’s base of operations, Vice City.

Sources indicate that as fans are aware, the new game returns to the setting of the 2002 release, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. Set in the 1980s, that game borrowed pretty heavily from the story of Brian De Palma’s brace of crime films Scarface and Carlito’s Way, giving players the ability to control one Tommy Vercetti as he rises from the streets to build a narcotics empire. As expected, disco, perms, neon signs and flared trousers were the order of the day.

Updated for 2026, GTA VI’s Vice City is a modern cityscape full of high-rises, trendy rooftop bars, nightclubs. and more. It sounds pretty idyllic, but this being GTA, there’s a shadier side, too. “When the sun fades and the neon glows, everyone has something to gain—and more to lose,” the official longline reads.

Industry observers note that the recent Netflix preview of the upcoming game gave us a bit more insight into the locale, including shots of BASE jumping from city bridges, a jewelry store robbery and subsequent high-speed escape, and a shootout through a drug den in a down-on-its-luck neighbourhood. In other words, as the main large city in the game, it looks like there’s plenty to keep Vice City residents occupied—on both sides of the law.

Industry observers note that inspiration: While Rockstar doesn’t explicitly explain that ‘game location X equals real world location Y’, it’s pretty obvious that Vice City is based on South Florida’s party capital, Miami. Despite the criminal element of Vice City, the real-world city has been keen to play on the connection. A Newly introduced York Times story suggests the city is keen to embrace its fictional twin due to a drastic drop in real-world crime recently. Which is, of course, great news for tourists. For the full GTA experience, you can enjoy Miami’s beaches, bars, and car culture, alongside iconic EDM nightspots like Club Space and E11EVEN Miami.

In Leonida Keys, the dress code is casual and the bars are loaded. “Life in this tropical archipelago isn’t flashy, but it’s easy,” runs the official description. In game, the Keys look like an ideal place to hit pristine tropical waters for a dive, jet ski, or scuba trip. Naturally, there seems to be a strong party boat presence too, with a Spring Break vibe. While we’re sure some absolute in-game carnage will take place there, at present, it actually looks like quite a nice place to unwind and escape the more criminal elements of the game’s plot.

Inspiration: The obvious IRL comp here is Key West, nestled at the very southern tip of Florida. In fact, here you can see the southernmost point in the continental US, just 90 miles from Cuba as the crow flies. As well as a plethora of luxury hotels, casual bars, and seafood spots, you can kick back on white beaches, or enjoy a glass-bottomed boat tour.

Recent findings suggest that for a break from all of this, you can visit the Hemingway Home, where Ernest Hemingway finished books including A Farewell to Arms and To Have and Have Not—that is, when he wasn’t out big-game fishing. The house is home to the first-ever swimming pool built in the Keys, as well as descendants of Hemingway’s famous six-toed cats.

Fans don’t know much about GTA 6’s Grassrivers yet, although the official synopsis does suggest some intrigue: “You never know what lies beneath the surface of this primordial expanse. The gators may be the most famous attraction, but there are far deadlier predators and weirder discoveries among the mangroves.” So far, all we’ve seen is an airboat tour and a birdwatching tower, suggesting a heavy emphasis on encounters with the natural world. Watch this space.

It has been revealed that inspiration: Clearly inspired by the Florida Everglades, Grassrivers will surely have a feel and flavor all of its own. The real Everglades has a rich cultural history. Yes, there are airboat tours catered to tourists during which you can spot ‘gators and learn all about the invasive pythons that are terrorising the ecosystem. And yes, you will be able to try deep-fried gator afterwards. But the real treasure is traditional foods like thick and chewy fry bread, swamp cabbage, or sofkee, a thin porridge made from corn.

And, at the Ah-Tah-Thi-Ki Museum near Fort Lauderdale in the north of the Everglades, you can learn about the Seminole nation, a group made up of Native Americans moving south to escape the British, mixed with escaped formerly enslaved peoples from the area’s plantations.

If GTA 6 were represented on an old-timey naval map, Port Gellhorn a “failed resort on the edge of the map" might be marked “here be monsters.”.

We know very little about the area yet, except for the fact that it’s rooted in poverty, with locals pushed to extremes to make ends meet. According to Rockstar, “Cheap motels, shut-down attractions and empty strip malls won’t bring the tourists back, but there’s a newly introduced economy in this once-popular vacation spot. It’s fuelled by malt liquor, painkillers and truck-stop energy drinks. Jump on a dirt bike and hold onto your wallet.” In other words, it sounds like a great place for a video game, less so for a holiday.

Industry observers note that inspiration: Again, Rockstar hasn’t been open about which area of Florida Port Gellhorn is based on, but fans and Florida locals think it takes inspiration from Panama City and the surrounding areas in the Florida Panhandle. Off the beaten track of most holidays, Panama City nevertheless has a strong reputation for seafood and water sports. Given its deepwater port, there’s also a strong maritime history. St Andrews State Park might be your best bet for snorkelling, swimming, kayaking and a calm and safe designated tidal pool.

In a recent development, ambrosia sounds, possibly, like the least appealing locale in GTA 6. It’s reportedly a factory town, overseen by vicious biker gangs. “In the heart of Leonida, American industry and old-school values still reign supreme – whatever the cost. The Allied Crystal sugar refinery provides the jobs, while the local biker gang provides almost everything else,” runs Rockstar’s official primer on the place. The Netflix preview didn’t help. We saw a shootout in a dilapidated house, backyard wrestling, and possibly some mud-wrestling too. Mark this one as the biggest unknown of the game.

In a recent development, inspiration: Florida locals think Ambrosia is based on Clewiston, Florida and the surrounding agricultural area around Lake Okeechobee. The main crop here is sugar, with Clewiston known as "America's Sweetest Town.” The irony in the in-game depiction is pretty obvious here, but the IRL location is well worth a visit if you’re a fan of fishing, with the local largemouth bass on Lake Okeechobee a particularly sought-after prize.

Recent findings suggest that mount Kalaga National Park looks like a truly beautiful in-game location, teeming with wildlife and activities from bicycle riding to kayaking. What’s not to love? Well, this bucolic utopia may actually prove to be too good to be true. In the Netflix preview, a televised advert for the ‘Prairie Sandwich’ seemed to take place in the park, suggesting that rather than enjoying the park’s animals in their natural habitat, your main goal might actually be to shoot them. If so, hunting will be an interesting addition to the game, and one that worked well in Red Dead Redemption 2. Of course, players will probably be able to opt out of the bloodshed and just enjoy a nice stroll among the trees instead. Here’s hoping.

Recent findings suggest that inspiration: While there’s no one-for-one comp for Mount Kalaga National Park, the Southern US States in particular are well known for their stunning national parks. Fans think this one takes inspiration from North Carolina’s Table Rock Mountain, Georgia’s Providence Canyon State Park, and the Suwannee River, which runs through Georgia and Florida. Whatever the real inspiration, if you are visiting Florida, it’s a reminder to get off the beaten path and out of the cities into lovingly preserved wild areas.

As the most discerning, up-to-the-minute voice in all things travel, Condé Nast Traveler is the global citizen’s bible and muse, offering both inspiration and vital intel. We understand that time is the greatest luxury, which is why Condé Nast Traveler mines its network of experts and influencers so that you never waste a meal, a drink, or a hotel stay wherever you are in the world.

#177. A TikToker Went Viral for Kayaking 500 Miles of Congolese River—and Started an Even Bigger Conversation

📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9 min read (1777 words)
General 🌐 Cntraveler

A TikToker Went Viral for Kayaking 500 Miles of Congolese River—and Started an Even Bigger Conversation

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read | Source: Cntraveler

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, last month the Welsh adventurer and self-described extreme athlete Ash Dykes was paddling along the placid waters of the Sangha River, a tributary of the Congo River flowing through Cameroon, Central African Republic, and Republic of the Congo, when something stirred underneath his vessel, kicking up bubbles.
  • In October, adventurer Ash Dykes, local guide Obed Temba Tuyumvire, and cameraman Will Perez embarked on a 500-mile kayaking trip in Republic of the Congo.
  • In a recent development, when Dykes posted the minute-and-a-half-long video of this “encounter” in the Sangha—cause still unknown—the post racked up over 8 million views on TikTok.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, last month the Welsh adventurer and self-described extreme athlete Ash Dykes was paddling along the placid waters of the Sangha River, a tributary of the Congo River flowing through Cameroon, Central African Republic, and Republic of the Congo, when something stirred underneath his vessel, kicking up bubbles. Dykes, with the local guide Obed Temba Tuyumvire and cameraman Will Perez, had just pushed off on a kayaking trip through the Congo Basin, the world’s second-largest rainforest and a critical ecosystem for humans and wildlife alike. The team knew they might encounter lowland gorillas, or perhaps forest elephants, as they made their way nearly 500 miles down the river. Perez then brought up another possible cause for the sudden ripples: a hippo. If the travelers had happened upon a hippopotamus, as many locals had warned them about, they were in immediate peril.

In October, adventurer Ash Dykes, local guide Obed Temba Tuyumvire, and cameraman Will Perez embarked on a 500-mile kayaking trip in Republic of the Congo.

In a recent development, when Dykes posted the minute-and-a-half-long video of this “encounter” in the Sangha—cause still unknown—the post racked up over 8 million views on TikTok. The thousands-deep comments section, full of viewers hooked as to what might happen next, burst with theories: Some swore that Mami Wata, a water spirit said to frequent the riverbanks, had caused the sudden movement. One user mused that the three men were in “a real game of Hungry Hungry Hippos,” while others zoomed in on Perez’s visibly tense expression. Another user quipped: “I quit my job to focus on this expedition.”.

Though intended as a joke, the latter reaction succinctly illustrates the attention this trip has garnered on social media. For weeks millions of viewers were glued to the team’s frequent TikTok dispatches—which they later fleshed out into a longer YouTube series of deep dives. The videos documented the logistical hurdles in reaching the Sangha; their trudging amid the heat and threat of parasites and disease; their day spent with the Ba’Aka people, a seminomadic Indigenous tribe in Dzanga-Sangha Protected Area, where they foraged for wild coconut and joined a traditional hunt; and extended stretches of the three bobbing through calm waters. Those following online celebrated alongside the men when they spotted forest elephants, and their pulses quickened when they outran a swarm of bees chasing their kayaks. When the team went abruptly silent for a prolonged stretch, following a power bank failure, viewers worried that something catastrophic had happened.

The Congo Basin is the world’s second-largest rainforest and a critical ecosystem for humans and wildlife alike.

Recent findings suggest that the Sangha expedition—or “mission,” as Dykes has dubbed it—was the first leg in an ambitious undertaking called Project 6. The venture involves the Welshman—who’s made a career of adventure travel and breaking world records (such as becoming the first person to walk the length of the 4,000-mile-long Yangtze River, which took him nearly a year)—traverse “extreme” parts of the globe by performing intensive feats of athleticism. He will soon cross Kyrgyzstan on horseback in subzero temperatures for the second installment of the project; he is revealing ensuing stops one by one.

In a recent development, “I'm fascinated with corners of the world that I am unfamiliar with and learning from the people there that call it home,” Dykes claims. “Then [it’s] mixed in with the challenge of: Can I do what is deemed impossible, or can I do what people have tried to do before but failed to complete?”.

Aside from accomplishing the athletic challenge of constantly paddling down the Sangha every day for weeks, Dykes notes he aimed to showcase the beauty of the Congo Basin, and its inhabitants, in a responsible way—stressing to viewers that “you can go to places like this as long as you put the right preparation in,” he says.

Video on TikTok and Youtube showed the trio of Tuyumvire, Perez, and Dykes on their river adventure.

It has been revealed that dykes is quick to credit those who made the Congo Basin excursion possible—especially Tuyumvire, who works in conservation advocacy and ecotourism through his Kigali-based company, Kumbukumbu Tours. Born in a forest village near Virunga National Park in the Democratic Republic of Congo, he fled the region following the civil war and lived in a refugee camp for over a decade before founding his tour company in 2015; he states those experiences shaped his belief that responsible tourism can be a means of helping make a local impact, particularly for young people. Tuyumvire agreed to join Dykes’s excursion because he saw an opportunity to tell meaningful stories about the Congo Basin for a larger audience.

Recent findings suggest that “Because we have been surviving these out-of-context stories or even more exaggerated stories,” says Tuyumvire. “I myself feel the responsibility to always say yes to someone who has the microphone, and I tell the right context.”.

Sources indicate that ahead of the excursion Tuyumvire worked with Dykes to pick the specific location for the journey and scouted out the upper headwaters of the Sangha. Tuyumvire offered context and commentary in videos throughout the trip, speaking about the critical endangerment of forest elephants, the deforestation threatening the Congo Basin, and noting that women were on the front lines of hunting when they met the Ba’Aka people.

In a recent development, yet straddling the line between education and entertainment for a predominantly TikTok viewership resulted in unexpected tensions. Internet connectivity posed a challenge due to the forest canopy; still, Dykes insisted the journey be “as live as possible” online. “I can’t be claiming that this is a lifetime expedition and then we use either recycled content or we go dark,” he states.

Forest elephants are among the wildlife that inhabits the Congo Basin through which the team traveled.

According to recent reports, while a plurality of viewers seemed genuinely fascinated by the three-week-long trip, even during less-exciting moments, Dykes noticed that some expressed a morbid glee for destructive content. Dykes indicates that some online commenters even started to bet money on how the trio might die in the Congo Basin, perhaps at the hands of a hippopotamus or a crocodile. “I think people are lost or confused as to what is a video game and what is a movie, and then what is reality,” he says. “So it's almost like this disconnect where people just wanted to be entertained: ‘If I'm going to the Congo, I want to see you escaping wildlife, wrestling.’” Tuyumvire saw the conflicting responses from viewers as “another kind of challenge for me to…create a story that will continuously be fed to the audience, but that will not also be overcrowded by too much exaggeration.”.

Recent findings suggest that others have criticized Dykes, drawing parallels between him and other foreigners entering so-called forbidding places and, intentionally or not, reinforcing outdated tropes. Guy Dieudonne Moukandi N'Kaya, a lecturer and researcher at Marien Ngouabi University in Brazzaville, Republic of the Congo, claims that Dykes’s trip through the Sangha felt honest in that it revealed the “tense coexistence” between humans and wildlife in the region. Yet the way Dykes framed the expedition gave N’Kaya pause: Leading up to the trip, Dykes noted in a TikTok teaser that he would be “dropping into the heart of darkness,” a phrase culled from Joseph Conrad’s controversial, turn-of-the-20th-century novella about a Belgian trading organization siphoning resources from the Congo River. N’Kaya says that descriptors such as “heart of darkness” and “unexplored,” which Dykes has also used in some of his posts, erase the presence of those who have long lived within the region: “The Sangha is not empty,” N’Kaya writes over email. “For centuries it has been traversed by people in dug-out canoes—fisherfolk, traders, and families.”.

The water of the Sangha River, a tributary of the Congo River, is tranquil—but the threat of disease-carrying bugs, dangerous wildlife, and the physical challenge of traveling 500 miles on human power made this one of Dykes' six missions.

According to recent reports, while Dykes emphasizes that he wanted to raise awareness of the Congo Basin, which is under dire threat of deforestation, some viewers have questioned whether the adventure has truly benefited the region—or whether it’s more of a boon to his Project 6 venture. The Congo Basin has long grappled with interlacing challenges including extreme poverty, corruption, and illegal mineral mining, which Tuyumvire claims stem from the legacy of colonialism and slavery. “People are poor in the sense that they are ready to sell anything they are able to, to be able to just survive,” Tuyumvire says. “People seeing a white person in this region, it brings memories of the past: ‘This guy’s coming for timber. This guy’s coming for minerals.’ Things that really don't give them any kind of hope to develop the area. And that itself, the mindset, is a threat to the forest.”.

It has been revealed that after returning from the trip in late October, Tuyumvire has been resting and resuming his routine following the physical demands of kayaking. He’d never kayaked at length before a few weeks ago; he claims his real motivation was to “share the stories and to try to transform the adventure into something impactful.” The widespread interest in the videos hasn't translated to bookings of his tours, but that was never the goal: “The audience we had is not an audience of travelers, to be honest,” he says. He has been reflecting on how, in hindsight, he wishes he had created a stronger call to action so that TikTok viewers’ curiosity could have a direct impact on the region. (Alongside his tours Tuyumvire helps run the Congo Rainforest Fund, a local NGO that works with local communities to understand threats to the forest and create solutions, such as shoring up educational efforts and job opportunities.).

But he believes that broadcasting the journey did help viewers further understand a place that they may not have been familiar with. “[The] Congo Basin has been represented as a difficult place to access, a difficult, complex place to understand,” Tuyumvire says. “So people were saying, ‘Finally, someone is going to give us the real information’…we want to see them in the reality.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that yesterday, we saw the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) problem a nationwide ground stop, which wasn’t fully lifted for over four hours. This represents the single biggest grounding of flights in the United States since 9/11, so the scale of whatever happened is pretty wild.

Industry observers note that at around 8PM last night, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin held a press conference to revision people on the state of things. I can’t help but cover this, because it felt like something between an SNL skit and a shakedown, and they couldn’t even keep their story straight… all while praising themselves for doing an unprecedented job!

Below you can find the press conference last night regarding the FAA shutdown, which happened around the time that the ground stop was lifted. First Mullin and Duffy spoke for around 10 minutes, and then they took questions for around 20 minutes.

The gist of the story is that they claim there were no signs of this being a cyber attack, and basically they broadly blame the outdated air traffic control system.

Mullin didn’t speak for long, and his primary comment was this:.

According to recent reports, “This is what the leadership of President Trump looks like, by the organization and team he has put together. We are built to handle crises like this, and that’s exactly what we’re doing. We’re moving at an unprecedented pace, as a whole of government, to make sure we’re doing the public justice by making sure everyone is safe, which everyone is.”.

Industry observers note that isn’t this a little self-congratulatory, especially while he’s also claiming that they don’t fully know the cause here? Just objectively, the pace was indeed unprecedented… it was the longest ground stop since 9/11!

Then you have Duffy speak, and this basically just turned into a demand for Congress to give him $50 billion to modernize our aviation infrastructure, while not actually being honest about the state of things:.

“The President, for the last year, has been asking Congress to fully fund a full build of a upcoming air traffic control system.”.

It has been revealed that that’s just not accurate at all. In July 2025, Congress authorized $12.5 billion for modernizing air traffic control, which Duffy described as a “down payment.” Since then, the size of the request kept changing, and the formal ask only went to Congress this week, when Duffy asked lawmakers for $30.1 billion for air traffic control and airport upgrades.

So it’s a bit rich to claim that Congress has been uncooperative over the past year, especially when you consider Republicans have controlled the White House, House, and Senate.

He then tried to explain what happened, which just feels like a complete deflection to me, as it’s about an overall need to modernize ATC, rather than what actually went wrong here:.

It has been revealed that “What happened is that our switches, actually got overloaded with data, and they went down… I shouldn’t say they went down… they started to give us inconsistency with the data from those routers, and because of that, we shut the system down. Now, I have already replaced some of those switches with President Trump, and our newly introduced IP switches did not go down. It’s the old hardware that went down, and I think the question for the American people is, ‘do you want your Congress to fund this?'”.

“I think the Congress at a point looked at the history of the FAA, and remarked ‘we don’t trust you.’ Well with President Trump, and what we’ve done, I think they do trust, because what we’ve done with that first tranche of money.”.

“I’ve asked the President to ask for $30 billion. I want $50 billion.”.

Obviously our air traffic control technology is really outdated and does need updating, there are no two ways about it. However, what was different yesterday, and caused an outage to this scale?

You can see I quoted Duffy above as saying that he claimed that “what happened is that our switches, actually got overloaded with data,” and that this caused the shutdown. I’m not a tech expert, but how exactly does that happen and cause the systems nationwide to have concerns? At most, you’d assume it would be regionalized, no?

So this is where the questions from reporters come in handy. Mullin seemingly threw Duffy under the bus, saying:.

“What it appears to be right now is that as Secretary Duffy and FAA was going in and putting patches in the system, they were putting fresh equipment, and new technology, and that new equipment and new technology was overwhelming the older system.”.

You can see Secretary Duffy’s reaction as Secretary Mullin indicates the newer technology was overwhelming the system. pic.twitter.com/IeoW5nM4aY.

According to recent reports, duffy was then asked what was different yesterday, given that the system had been in place for years. As you’d expect, there was no good answer.

Initially Duffy made it sound like they knew exactly what happened, but then he backtracked on that, and said “we’re still working on the details of what went wrong, I’ll be happy to give you more information, but I don’t want to give you the wrong information.”.

Very good set of questions from Luke Radel for Secretary Duffy and Secretary Mullin. pic.twitter.com/f6tlfDtbJG.

It has been revealed that I also appreciate how someone actually asked the question about this being blamed on Congress, given that the Republicans have had full control for the past two years. As you’d expect, Duffy’s response was first to ask what network the person was from.

DUFFY: How many times does this have to happen before congress gives the money to fix it?R: You’ve been in office almost two years now, Republicans controlled both chambers of congress and still do.DUFFY: What your network are you from? pic.twitter.com/xuX5arTwjl.

What’s amazing to me is the overall tone of the press conference. They feel bad for themselves, with Duffy pointing out that he hopes he doesn’t have to give another press conference after 8PM. You know what’s not mentioned once, though? Thanking travelers for their patience throughout all of this, or apologizing to the public for the disruption. Not once.

In a recent development, I’m 100% in support of funding and modernizing air traffic control. But when you have the biggest outage you’ve had in over 25 years, it seems a bit rich to say “give us $50 billion” and “we’re doing an unprecedented job.” And again, if Mullin is to be believed, the system updates that were put in place were to blame.

Breaking – All flights nationwide have beengrounded – the #FAA is facing a computer outage.Yet another major blow to incompetent Transportation Sect Mayor Pete and people who get vital jobs with no experience to check some identity politics boxes.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin held a press conference last night about the nationwide ground stop, and it just struck me as being incredibly tone deaf and off base.

It has been revealed that you had Mullin congratulating the Trump administration for their “unprecedented” response, you had Duffy claiming the outage was due to switches getting overloaded with data, and you had had Mullin then claim this happened because of the system updates that Duffy put in place. Oh, and the focus was also on demanding that Congress give them $50 billion, suggesting they’ve been dragging their feet for the past year.

There was zero tone of accountability or apology. There was no “thanks to everyone traveling for their patience,” but instead, self-pity for the fact that they had to be there after 8PM on a Friday, when they’d probably rather be at home… or a bar, maybe.

#175. How Much Wider Is The Boeing 787's Fuselage Compared To The 767?

📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7 min read (1483 words)
General 🌐 Simpleflying

How Much Wider Is The Boeing 787's Fuselage Compared To The 767?

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read | Source: Simpleflying

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that boeing built both the 767 and 787 to serve similar roles, albeit decades apart.
  • Recent findings suggest that but passenger comfort is another matter, and whether one aircraft offers a better experience for those on board than the other is somewhat debatable when it comes to the 767 and 787.
  • As to how much wider it is, the short answer is: Significantly enough.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that boeing built both the 767 and 787 to serve similar roles, albeit decades apart. Each is an example of a twin-engine widebody designed to serve medium- to long-haul routes, but at a fraction of the cost of more fuel-hungry quadjets. Naturally, the newer technology available when the 787 — or Dreamliner as it is known — was built means it trumps its older counterpart in efficiency and range.

Recent findings suggest that but passenger comfort is another matter, and whether one aircraft offers a better experience for those on board than the other is somewhat debatable when it comes to the 767 and 787. No doubt, the 787 has the edge in several areas. Fuselage width, however, does not necessarily work in its favor, despite the 787 offering more space in this sense than the 767.

As to how much wider it is, the short answer is: Significantly enough. The 787’s fuselage measures an extra two feet, five inches (0.74 meters) in width than the 767’s. Internally, the distance between each cabin wall is a slightly more moderate two feet, four inches (0.71 meters) greater aboard the 787 than the 767. That applies to all variants within the respective 787 and 767 families, given that each set of aircraft shares a common cross-section.

Although the differences cited above may appear marginal, they do have very real ramifications for airlines and passengers alike. With an interior trim-to-trim width of 15 feet, six inches (4.72 meters), the 767 allows for rows of seven abreast economy seats laid out in a 2-3-2 configuration, according to Boeing aircraft characteristics documents. Each walkway running down the cabin is stated to measure one foot, seven inches (0.48 meters) across.

Boeing 767 and 787 family fuselage cross-section widths:.

Industry observers note that in contrast, the 787’s internal cabin width of 18 feet (5.49 meters) means enough space is available for airlines to fit rows of nine economy seats in a 3-3-3 configuration. Its walkways also measure a slightly smaller one foot, six inches (0.46 meters) in the standard cabin, per the Boeing documents. All of that goes to say, the 787 does boast a wider fuselage and internal cabin, but that does not necessarily translate to more room per passenger onboard.

Beyond space per passenger, in economy seating at least, the 787 trumps the 767 on pretty much every other metric. Boeing officially rolled out the Dreamliner program in 2004, well after the 767’s own introduction. Come 2011, when the 787 debuted commercially with All Nippon Airways, the airliner was unlike anything that had come before it.

Industry observers note that instead of relying so heavily on traditional materials such as aluminum, Boeing primarily built the 787s out of carbon fiber composites. Such materials, which are lighter and more resistant to corrosion, make up roughly 50% of the aircraft by weight, according to the manufacturer. That means “less fuel to lift, cruise, climb and maneuver,” as Boeing writes. Coupled with improved aerodynamics and newer engine technology, that translates to a 25% reduction in fuel burn compared to the planes the 787 was intended to replace.

Boeing 787 family specifications, from Boeing:.

GE Aerospace GEnx-1B / Rolls-Royce Trent 1000.

GE Aerospace GEnx-1B / Rolls-Royce Trent 1000.

GE Aerospace GEnx-1B / Rolls-Royce Trent 1000.

According to recent reports, but the wide use of composites in the 787 has offered benefits beyond just improved efficiency. For passengers, dehydration and jet lag are common effects of long-haul flights. Boeing was able to incorporate features into the 787 to mitigate both, though. Given that carbon composites do not rust, cabin humidity levels can be kept higher in the newer-generation widebody. Similarly, fatigue-resistant properties allow a lower cabin altitude—which plays a large part in the severity of jet lag—to be maintained than on older aluminum aircraft.

The Dreamliner achieves its fuel efficiency and range flexibility through advanced materials, aerodynamics, and smart design.

In contrast, the 767 is very much a product of its time. Developed alongside the Boeing 757, the 767 program was officially debuted back in 1978. The widebody then made its first commercial flight with United Airlines in 1982. Needless to say, technology moved on a fair bit in the near-three-decade gap between the 767 and 787’s respective entries into service.

According to recent reports, as with many aging models built primarily from aluminum, the 767’s cabin altitude tends to sit in the 7,000- to 8,000-feet (2,137 to 2,439-meter) range. That is cut to 6,000 feet (1,829 meters) on the 787, meaning passengers experience a smaller drop in blood oxygen saturation—which itself contributes to classic jet-lag symptoms. Humidity in the 767 and older jets’ cabins can also drop below 10%, deliberately to stave off corrosion. Aboard the 787, moisture is less of a worry, so humidity tends to be higher, at between 15% and 25%, contributing to a more comfortable experience for those onboard.

Select Boeing 767 family specifications, from Flightradar24 and Boeing:.

Pratt & Whitney JT9D / Pratt & Whitney PW4000 / General Electric CF6.

Pratt & Whitney JT9D / Pratt & Whitney PW4000 / General Electric CF6 / Rolls-Royce RB211.

Pratt & Whitney JT9D / Pratt & Whitney PW4000 / General Electric CF6 / Rolls-Royce RB211.

Pratt & Whitney PW4000 / General Electric CF6.

It has been revealed that no doubt, Boeing built the 787 to trump its predecessors across the board on efficiency and passenger comfort. The irony is that, in offering a cabin that was wider and more spacious than the 767’s, Boeing effectively gave airlines the choice of squeezing in more seats or giving passengers the extra room. As it turned out, airlines almost universally opted to use the extra width for capacity.

Indeed, Boeing reportedly originally intended the 787 to seat eight passengers per row in economy, in a 2-4-2 configuration. Instead, the 3-3-3 layout has become favored by most airlines. That means it is on the 767, which tends to seat economy travelers in a 2-3-2 pattern, where space is more abundant—despite its narrower fuselage.

United, as an operator of both the 787 and 767, offers a clear example of this. Economy seat width — measured from the inner sides of armrests — across its Dreamliner fleet ranges from approximately 16.6 inches (42.2 centimeters) to 17.6 inches (44.7 centimeters) depending on model and specific interior, per the carrier’s website. Aboard its 767s, this varies between 18.0 inches (45.7 centimeters) and 18.5 inches (47.0 centimeters).

Boeing 767 and Boeing 787 deliveries to date, from Boeing data:.

Of course, seat pitch and recline also play a part in determining how much room each passenger gets, and similarly vary from carrier to carrier. That said, the trend of economy seats being wider on 767s than 787s is not limited to United; most carriers put the latter’s wider fuselage to work by installing extra seats.

How do the two airliners differ, and what sets them apart from older aircraft?

In a recent development, not all do, though. Japan Airlines is a notable exception when it comes to the 787, given its Dreamliner economy cabins feature a seat less per row than at the majority of other carriers. Unsurprisingly, this means the airline’s standard 787 seats are wider than those on its 767s.

Based on figures from the Japanese flag carrier’s website, passengers can expect their economy seat to measure approximately 18.9 inches (48 centimeters) from the inside of one armrest to the other if on one of its 787s. Conversely, this drops to around 17.7 inches (45 centimeters) aboard Japan Airlines’ 767s.

This is because, unlike others, the carrier’s 787s host a 2-4-2 instead of a 3-3-3 configuration in their main cabins. As the airline writes itself: “A more relaxed eight-across seat layout rather than the industry standard nine-across [allows] for an extra five centimeters in seat width.” Compared to Japan Airlines’ 767s, which use the usual 2-3-2 main cabin layout, more of the extra space afforded by the 787’s wider cabin goes to passengers.

All told, Japan Airlines is an outlier when it comes to its 787 seating plan. The bulk of airlines have instead taken to getting the maximum out of the Dreamliner’s width by fitting more passengers per row than on the 767. In other words, the fact that the 787 offers more space between cabin walls does not necessarily mean a more spacious seat onboard in most cases.

There is also the noteworthy fact that 767s tend to feature just one middle seat across each main cabin row. That is impressive not only compared to the 787, but also to even bulkier jets like the Boeing 777, where economy passengers will usually find ten adjacent seats laid out in a 3-4-3 formation.

#173. What’s My Lebensphilosophie? I Went to the Austrian Alps to Find Out

📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12 min read (2381 words)
General 🌐 Cntraveler

What’s My Lebensphilosophie? I Went to the Austrian Alps to Find Out

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read | Source: Cntraveler

💡 Key Takeaways
  • When I was told the general rule of thumb at Hotel Nesslerhof, an alpine wellness resort nestled in Austria’s Großarl Valley, was that it’s weird if you’re not naked, I listened.
  • In Austria, being naked isn’t just a physical state.
  • Großarl Valley, also known as the “Valley of Alpine Pastures" in the Salzburger Land region of Austria.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When I was told the general rule of thumb at Hotel Nesslerhof, an alpine wellness resort nestled in Austria’s Großarl Valley, was that it’s weird if you’re not naked, I listened.

In Austria, being naked isn’t just a physical state. It’s an emotional state, too. Austrians strip themselves down, both figuratively and literally, to achieve a mindset they call “Lebensgefühl,” a deep mind-body awareness and lifestyle that is difficult to define, let alone translate.

Großarl Valley, also known as the “Valley of Alpine Pastures" in the Salzburger Land region of Austria.

Industry observers note that originally a German concept, the idea stems from “Lebensphilosophie,” a 19th-century intellectual movement popularized by big name thinkers like Friedrich Nietzsche, Georg Simmel, and Wilhelm Dilthey. Translating to “philosophy of life,” the framework is centered around the idea that life can only be understood from within oneself, as opposed to through applying external dogmas like logic and science. Life, according to this framework, is a joyful, vibrant, and embodied experience—a philosophy now widely integrated and cherished by Germany’s neighbor, Austria.

Language, of course, falls short when attempting to describe what Lebensgefühl means in practice; this complete awareness of being is a physicality, an emotion, a lifestyle, and a philosophy all rolled into one. It can’t be described, only felt (ah!). It’s the pleasure of simply existing. Leben (life), Gefühl (feeling). It’s an experience I wanted to understand firsthand. So when I found myself in Munich, less than a two-hour train ride from Hotel Nesslerhof, with a lifelong friend oblivious to my schemes, I decided it was time to get to the bottom of it.

The root of Lebensgefühl is being entirely present in a moment: a conscious effort to slow down, gauge your own energy in the here and now, and choose the way you want to live your life accordingly. While the Austrian National Tourist Board uses the concept of Lebensgefühl as a marketing language, the feeling itself is real–and you can cultivate it anywhere. Admittedly, though—hand of accountability raised—it’s a whole lot easier when you’re surrounded by the postcard-perfect Austrian Alps.

Reaching this state of awareness requires an analog attention span and total presence. This is exactly what is demanded of you at Hotel Nesslerhof, which has dubbed itself the “natural happiness hotel.” The sprawling, sun-warmed property is an emerald-colored garden punctured by buttery blonde oak 1643 Austrian longhouse architecture. Here, the world is calm. Quiet.

I arrive burned out, my attention scattered across screens and obligations. Stepping into a place fully immersed in nature with nothing expected of me, is jarring. It's been a while since I've consumed life this way. We’re conditioned to scroll, desire, save, project, and imagine, rather than to simply be—even to just be for a little bit.

Industry observers note that finding the answer started with carving out time and space, and letting go of everything I thought presence was supposed to look like. Next thing, I was naked in Austria with 40 strangers wondering the same thing.

Natural swimming pond for post-sauna plunges in the Zwanzigsechzehn sauna area for guests aged 16 and older.

The hotel’s dedicated wellness area features five co-ed clothing-optional saunas (plus an additional private sauna in select suites), a salt steam bath, infrared loungers, and expansive natural swimming pools. To practice, or fully embody, Lebensgefühl successfully, you must be aware of your environment. At Nesslerhof, the alpine nature allows your body to break away from any externally imposed schedules and return back to your natural circadian rhythm, where an omniscient digital third person doesn't determine your flow; you do.

A Swiss pine sauna in the Zwanzigsechzehn sauna area for guests aged 16 and older.

As a lifelong advocate for a good time, I mustered some gumption to join one of the daily themed sauna “infusions.” During these sessions, a sauna master leads thematic experiences using natural, regional botanicals like thyme, sage, Swiss stone pine, and eucalyptus. It’s held in the adults-only sauna event room, a space large enough to accommodate nearly 50 people.

Industry observers note that I walk in—towel on—and it occurs to me I’m the one making it weird here. There’s a lot I can swallow in life, but one thing I certainly will not do is be the person making things weird in a room. So, I lose the towel, join the crowd, and, in a state of mild panic, take a seat on the floor. Now, retrospectively speaking, I couldn’t grasp how all my choices in life had led me to this single, very conscious state of nudity in front of 40 Austrian strangers. There I was—sitting on the floor, completely floored. Which actually made things weirder, because I was later told you aren’t supposed to sit on the floor.

Enter the sauna master. Also nude. A sauna master is like a spiritual guide to a proper schvitz, and the infusions at Nesslerhof are next level material. At pivotal moments, I’m watching him execute rainbow ice acrobatics, teasing large, colorful chunks of ice around the room in a giant spoon before launching them onto the glowing-hot stones. Steam is sizzling everywhere as thick aromatics sweep across the room.

Hotel Nesslerhof's outdoor saltwater pool (with indoor access) surrounded by the Großarl Valley.

Sources indicate that and it’s hot. To make matters worse for myself—still on the floor—we’re given a natural body scrub to apply. So, whatever, sure: I start scrubbing amidst the rainbow ice, dense botanical air, and naked strangers unabashedly sprawled across the room in their entirety. I begin to gain consciousness of the palpable sense of self-assurance emanating from everyone as they laughed and chatted heart-to-heart. They were all having…fun. Slowly, decidedly, I reach a state of compos mentis: the only thing mortifying about this experience is my belief that this is a mortifying experience. This is not an intimidating reality. In fact, it’s pretty funny—and wildly inclusive, despite the fact that no one here speaks English but me. For the first time since arriving here, I feel entirely in the moment, free from any pressure to make it something else. I’m there, existing. I watch as my friend walks by the glass door and we lock eyes—him sending a distress call, and me, now a part of the sauna hijinks, completely in on the bit. Yeah, we’re all naked. So what?

Over the next three days, I continue this conversation with myself about the humility of physical form, alternating between stone pine saunas and crystal-clear mountain ponds. One amber afternoon, as I float between lily pads dotted by flowers and busy dragonflies, I stare at the burgeoning purple-pink Austrian Alps blanketing me, and I remember what it’s like to feel small again. Perception, both of ourselves and from others, has never really been that serious, has it? This is the body that’s given me life, the body that makes everything I do possible. Suddenly, I’m aware of every inch, from my fingertips to my toes. And I’m aware of my awareness. Lebensgefühl, for sure.

Mid-mind-body connection, a group of Austrian regulars hand-signals for me to come over for a beer. “For the electrolytes” is their roundabout scientific mojo after two to three courses of saunas and plunges. I catch what feels like an illegal glimpse of myself in the reflection of a sauna door and laugh. Gratitude emerges.

Hotel Nesslerhof's 800 m² natural swimming pond surrounded by a sunbathing lawn.

Gratitude for your body means food is more than just fuel, it’s an offering. The art of a meal has been a ritualistic practice since we were homo erectus: slowing down to practicing eating as an experience, not a function. And an eating environment can communicate a lot: savor this, stay with me, I’m here.

At Nesslerhof, eating was a slow and meditative practice, always beginning with a dedicated space: a seat at their table that was mine for my entire visit, an altar of sorts. Libations aplenty. In Austria, the Vorspeisensuppe—the traditional first-course soup—is served before almost every meal as a ceremonial anchor of hospitality and warmth. It’s often a non-negotiable, and acts as a symbolic moment to ground yourself before eating, or, as I’m practicing as an honorary Austrian here, to ground myself in a state of Lebensgefühl. For breakfast, lunch, dinner, and even the occasional snack, the soup is served first, and my brain instantly locks into being entirely in the moment. How could I not—I’m sipping on fresh ginger, carrot, and seasonal herb soups pulled directly from the mountains of Großarl—the lush valley an hour outside of Salzburg where the property sits.

Daily breakfast spread by the “Gästeflüsterer” team, including a wide selection of regional specialties.

Austrian Zwiebelrostbraten (pan-seared beef roast with crispy fried onions) served with seasonal Alpine accompaniments from the Großarl Valley.

Industry observers note that when you are sick, what do you feed yourself to get better? How do people care for you using food? A lot of roads lead back to soup. It’s nourishing, easy for a strained body to digest, and a slow, intentional practice. It’s an antidote to hurriedness, a gateway to culinary Lebensgefühl.

According to recent reports, outside of the soup, a daily breakfast and lunch menu of fresh regional dishes, served on a strict schedule in the main parlor, makes indecision obsolete. In the evening, a five-course dinner at Atelier N, the hotel’s dedicated dining space, feels like stepping into an Austrian grandmother’s kitchen and hitting all the classics: Perftillbauer lamb, roast venison, fried veal Butterschnitzel, and pan-fried fish fillets. Everything is local, organic, and rooted in a genuine "nose-to-tail" principle—completely free of pretentious trends. And everyone here is known by their first name. The baker, Toni, brings fresh bread and pastries every morning. Elisabeth crafts the butter, curd cheese, yogurt, and whey—a real lactose lady. Anni and Sepp Inhög’s bees live on the sunniest side of the valley, which means their honey is something else entirely. Fresh local salmon trout, rainbow trout, brook trout, Arctic char, and local game are sourced directly from the nearby Hohe Tauern National Park. It’s a literal "alp-to-table" dining experience.

Kreuzkogel mountain in the Großarl Valley, accessed by the Kieserlbahn cable car.

The writer stopping for wild blueberries on a hike in the Austrian Alps.

Recent findings suggest that hotel Nesslerhof's hospitality was the last dance to Lebensgefühl. Longing for an escape–more often than not–coincides with a longing to feel in touch with yourself again. A weltanschauung, or worldview, can easily become skewed by the monotony of everyday life, which is why it takes displacement to course-correct. Human connection—which in this case took the form of the warm hospitality of Nesslerhof's staff—can serve as the intermediary. An agent [what do you that can create safe third spaces, and abstractly direct you to where your values lie.

On a hike just outside Nesslerhof’s front door in Hohe Tauern National Park, I meet one of Hotel Nesslerhof’s owners, Tina Neudegger. She built the property from the ground up with her husband, Hermann, and their three daughters. That’s over 40 years of family tradition and expertise coursing through this space. Tina is a consumingly luminous person, a natural caregiver. What she fosters at the property extends beyond hospitality–it’s a sense of security. It’s a maternal, comforting awareness that I am entirely taken care of, that my environment is safe, and that I don’t need to be on the defense. At Nesslerhof, I receive the same attention she gives her daughters and her husband, who treat the hotel like their home because, well, it is their home.

In a recent development, employing my primate purpose, step by step with Tina as I teeter along an intimidating alpine cliffside, and attempting to eat a handful of fresh berries I covertly hoarded from a wily bush because I couldn't stop myself, I tune into her flow. We talk about how life can be a comedy of errors, and how we as humans cling to a gravitas that seems funny from a higher perspective. “Life’s simple. You can do anything once, right? So do it,” is Tina’s cheeky motto, something that makes all the seriousness in the world abruptly fade. I’m arrested by the smell of cows and am drawn back to the present. Weirdly, I like it.

The writer above Großarl Valley with Austrian libation.

The August 2026 total solar eclipse dips behind the Austrian Alps.

Industry observers note that later, Tina drives me up the mountain to watch the solar eclipse from Wolke7, her family’s ski lodge, which is normally reached by the Kieserlbahn cable car adjacent to the hotel. We’re on a 40-minute, long, winding road up the Austrian Alps that feels alarmingly close to vertical. I’m bearing intense witness to the fact that there’s no guardrail, but I'm at ease knowing I can free my gaze because of Tina's confidence. We continue on a path that’s already there, a path that's always been there, a path that will always be there. Something about that feels nice. At the summit, I meet the family she’s created in Großarl: her eclectic collection of friends who uphold this alpine town's legacy. They look at her with complete adoration as they pass me homemade Kaiserschmarrn and a Radler. We watch the eclipse slowly fade behind the Austrian Alps—the totality of it lasting just over two minutes.

But as I stand there, witnessing the world in its most sublime form, surrounded by Tina’s friends, who are vivid, complex, and completely magnanimous, the awe I feel expands from my chest, and those two minutes feel endless. I dub Tina the Mayor of Großarl, and as I overlook her valley, 6,500 meters above sea level, I see the whole picture again. At its deepest level, Lebensgefühl–your Lebensphilosophie–is painfully simple. What made you feel alive today? Build the environment for it. Pause and marvel. Continue forward.

#172. Delta 360: Benefits & How To Earn This Invitation-Only Status

📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8 min read (1571 words)
General 🌐 Onemileatatime

Delta 360: Benefits & How To Earn This Invitation-Only Status

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read | Source: Onemileatatime

💡 Key Takeaways
  • All of the “significant three” carriers in the United States have invitation-only elite status.
  • It has been revealed that what is Delta 360 status, how do you earn it, what are the benefits, and how many members are there?
  • Industry observers note that delta 360 is Delta Air Lines’ invitation-only elite status.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

All of the “significant three” carriers in the United States have invitation-only elite status. I’ve written about how American has Concierge Key and United has Global Services, and in this post, I’d like to take a look at Delta 360, which is Delta’s invitation-only elite status. I’d argue it’s the most mysterious, least talked about, and perhaps the rarest, of the three.

It has been revealed that what is Delta 360 status, how do you earn it, what are the benefits, and how many members are there? I’ll share everything I know….

Industry observers note that delta 360 is Delta Air Lines’ invitation-only elite status. It’s my understanding that this is the most exclusive of the invitation-only elite tiers, in the sense that there are the fewest members. Despite that, the benefits are actually pretty weak, at least on paper. For that matter, Delta 360 isn’t even a formal elite tier, which is to say that you separately still have to qualify for status in the Delta SkyMiles Medallion program.

For what it’s worth, here’s how Delta describes Delta 360 status on its website:.

Sources indicate that delta 360° is an annual, invitation-only membership for our most loyal SkyMiles Members. A Delta 360° Membership offers Delta’s most premium suite of benefits and services exclusive to our top SkyMiles Members. Entry into Delta 360° will be extended to a very small percentage of Diamond Medallion Members. Considerations include, but are not limited to: overall Delta flight activity, premium product purchases (Delta One, Delta Premium Select, Delta First) and spending on Delta SkyMiles American Express Cards.

As is the case with the invitation-only status of American and United, the requirements to earn Delta 360 status aren’t published. However, based on the data points I’ve seen, the criteria are even more confusing. With American and United, as a general rule, you need to spend well over $50,000 per year to have a shot at the status. In the case of Delta, you probably need to spend even more.

As Delta officially states, getting an invitation to Delta 360 is for the “most loyal SkyMiles members.” Generally speaking:.

Some suggest that you’d have to spend $100,000 per year on Delta flights to be invited as a Delta 360 member at major hubs, while the number could be much lower if you’re not based at a hub.

It has been revealed that note that qualification for Delta 360 is annual (so it expires at the end of the elite year), and criteria could change year-to-year. So it’s possible you have the same activity in two years, and earn Delta 360 one year, but not the other. There’s also no way to ask for or request the status (at least not in a way that will achieve the intended result). Instead, you’ll be contacted if you’re eligible, and you’ll see your account updated to reflect that.

There’s one other way to earn Delta 360 status. As part of the SkyMiles lifetime elite status program, you can receive Delta 360 status for life if you rack up five million lifetime miles. This metric is based on the number of eligible miles flown on Delta.

Sources indicate that just for some context on all of this, Delta’s top published tier is Diamond Medallion, and that requires earning 28,000 Medallion Qualifying Dollars (MQDs) in a program year. That would require $28,000 in spending on Delta tickets, or $280,000 to $560,000 in spending on select co-branded Delta credit cards.

In a recent development, interestingly, Delta 360 isn’t a separate tier in the SkyMiles program. That’s to say that Delta 360 members still have to earn status in the SkyMiles Medallion program. Most Delta 360 members are also Diamond Medallion members, but in theory it’s possible to earn Delta 360 without being a Diamond Medallion member.

This is different than American AAdvantage and United MileagePlus, where Concierge Key and Global Services are separate tiers, above the published top tier levels.

What are the benefits of Delta 360 status?

Those are all the Delta 360 benefits that I’m aware of. There’s no upgrade priority for Delta 360 members beyond their standard Diamond Medallion status, so Delta 360 doesn’t factor into upgrade priority. Furthermore, any confirmed upgrades would be earned through the standard Choice Benefits program, as this is how you can earn Global Upgrade Certificates (GUCs) and Regional Upgrade Certificates (RUCs).

So the benefits of Delta 360 are weak, though I’d imagine that the “soft” treatment is very good — Delta has great service to begin with, and I imagine it’s even better for Delta’s best customers.

In a recent development, I also think it’s noteworthy how Delta is much quieter about this status than American and United. There’s just not as much public acknowledgement of invitation only status at Delta as at American and United (and that might be by design).

This is a real mystery, and all I can do is speculate. For context, I’ve speculated that there are 10,000-20,000 American Concierge Key members, and I’ve speculated that there are 15,000-25,000 United Global Services members.

It has been revealed that this is purely a guess on my part, but I think the number of Delta 360 members is probably in the 5,000-10,000 range. That’s simply because the status seems to be more difficult to earn. Like I stated, this is purely a guess on my part, and I could be wrong. If anyone has any data or info, I’d love to hear it.

In a recent development, it’s hard to say whether something like Delta 360 is “worth it.” For one, the qualification requirements aren’t even published, so how can one say whether it’s worth it when you don’t know what it will take? Second, I’d say the value of something like Delta 360 varies greatly based on the type of traveler you are.

Industry observers note that if you’re a domestic road warrior doing 200 segments per year, you might actually get significant upside from the improved assistance during irregular operations, the Delta One Lounge access, etc. Meanwhile if you take a handful of international long haul business class trips per year, the upside will likely be very minimal, above and beyond what you’d otherwise get.

Sources indicate that so I absolutely don’t think it’s worth going out of your way to try to earn something that doesn’t even have published qualification requirements. But if you earn it anyway, of course, it’s a nice thing to have!

The “major three” US carriers all have their own invitation-only elite status, with other programs including American Concierge Key and United Global Services. So how do they all compare?

It has been revealed that the reality is that all three tiers are primarily about better improved “soft” treatment, including during irregular operations. On paper, I’d say Delta 360 probably offers the fewest official perks of the three tiers. The one exception is that Delta One Lounge access is an absolutely awesome benefit, given the quality of lounges (though the lack of free guests limits the usefulness for those not usually traveling alone).

Here are a couple of thoughts on the comparable status tiers at American and United:.

It has been revealed that delta 360 is Delta Air Lines’ invitation-only elite tier. It’s the US airline status that’s probably hardest to earn. Historically the benefits have been weaker than comparable status with American and United, though with access to Delta One Lounges, that’s perhaps no longer the case. Delta 360 offers dedicated customer support, a Sky Club membership, Delta One Lounge access, good odds of tarmac transfers, and more.

To earn Delta 360, be prepared to spend a lot on Delta flights, especially if you’re based out of a Delta hub.

Recent findings suggest that are any OMAAT readers Delta 360 members? If so, what has your experience been like?

Membership is free and takes no more information than commenting as a guest. Earn status points for good contributions, and see fewer ads as your status grows.

#170. United CEO Scott Kirby Says “100%” Chance Merger With American Airlines Would Get Approved

📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 25 min read (4996 words)
Business & Policy 🌐 Viewfromthewing

United CEO Scott Kirby Says “100%” Chance Merger With American Airlines Would Get Approved

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read | Source: Viewfromthewing

💡 Key Takeaways
  • United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby says he’s “100%” convinced a merger with American Airlines could get approved.
  • It has been revealed that but ‘get approved’ doesn’t mean what he seems to suggest.
  • “We’d have to do some divestitures, but I 100% think it could get approved.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby says he’s “100%” convinced a merger with American Airlines could get approved. He says he’s even more confident than he was this spring, when news of the talks came out, and he sees getting American to agree as the biggest obstacle. But ‘get approved’ doesn’t mean what he seems to suggest. A friendly Justice Department signing off would still leave any such combination with state attorneys general, foreign governments and two competing sets of international airline partnerships to deal with. Speaking at Yahoo Finance Invest, Kirby said: “It wouldn’t be easy.” “We’d have to do some divestitures, but I 100% think it could get approved.” His argument is that bringing United’s service, technology and operational performance to more passengers would make them better off. He thinks critics misunderstand the deal because they treat airline seats as interchangeable. Contra Kirby, better service is actually a core part of DOJ merger guidelines recognizing quality, innovation and choice. Plus, United service isn’t that good! And while their operations are better than they used to be, they aren’t industry-leading. They’re consistently modestly better than American’s but the difference is hardly vast. Kirby Hasn’t Given Up On The Airline That Fired Him When I covered Kirby’s merger pitch in April, the appeal to United was obvious: American would give them a much bigger Upcoming York presence, more strength in Los Angeles, a southeastern hub and a powerful Latin America network. Kirby later said he’d build a Miami hub if he could get 40 or 50 gates. He also wants more at New York JFK than United’s planned return will provide. American rejected merger discussions, arguing that combining the airlines would hurt consumers and competition. Any antitrust case – even at the state level – would just quote American’s own release. As I covered October 31, Kirby described conversations he thought were continuing until American blindsided him with that press release. In any case, American can make investments without being bought. They’ve already made real progress over the past 21 months towards improving their product almost across-the-board. The Justice Department Doesn’t Get The Only Vote I laid out the problems beyond Washington back in April. Getting the administration to support a deal isn’t even close to enough. States can bring their own case. A federal settlement doesn’t bind state attorneys general who aren’t parties to it. Private plaintiffs can sue, too. The Clayton Act allows injunctions against threatened antitrust harm. Closing doesn’t automatically end the risk. The merger notification statute preserves later challenges. Letting the federal waiting period expire isn’t permanent antitrust immunity. He’d Have To Untangle Two Competing Global Networks American and US Airways needed European Commission clearance for their merger. The London–Philadelphia remedy included slots for a competing daily flight. Two U.S. companies combining doesn’t make the transaction solely an American matter. United and American also have joint ventures that let them coordinate prices, schedules and revenue with different foreign airlines. Among those arrangements: Market United’s Partners American’s Partners Atlantic   Lufthansa Group and Air Canada   British Airways, Iberia, Aer Lingus and Finnair Japan   All Nippon Airways   Japan Airlines South Pacific   Air New Zealand   Qantas A combined airline couldn’t assume it could keep these competing arrangements unchanged. Moving American’s flying into United’s partnerships would change the competition analysis. Ending American’s existing deals would also change the connecting traffic and economics Kirby is buying. The Transportation Department’s alliance approvals are another process, separate from Justice Department merger review. And foreign oversight is already an issue: Britain. American’s existing Atlantic partnership already faces slot remedies for London–Boston, London–Chicago and London–Miami, plus protections for London–Dallas passengers. In February, the British competition authority announced approved slot agreements for Delta on Boston and Virgin Atlantic on Miami. Buying American could create new hurdles for either transatlantic joint venture the combined carrier participated in. The European Union would have its own merger review, too. Japan. United and American have separate immunized partnerships with Japan’s two major network airlines. The merger would also raise questions about their scarce Tokyo Haneda access. Japan might not approve a combined American and United in either partnership. Keeping both carriers’ Haneda slots aren’t necessarily in the DOT’s view of the public interest. Australia and New Zealand. Australia renewed the American–Qantas alliance authorization on October 14. New Zealand renewed it in March, and separately authorizes United’s cooperation with Air New Zealand. Combining the American partners in those competing relationships would give both governments new questions to consider regardless of which airline they decided they wanted to keep a partnership with. Canada. United and Air Canada announced an expanded transborder agreement last month and submitted it to Transport Canada for approval. Combining that operation with American’s Canada seems almost impossible on its own. What Would United Have To Give Up? Chicago is the biggest domestic problem. United and American operate competing hubs at O’Hare. New York, Los Angeles and Washington raise challenges as well. United has Newark while American considers the combined LaGuardia and JFK a hub; both airlines have hubs at LAX, and United has a hub at Washington Dulles while American is the dominant carrier at Washington National. And surely American’s debt is a poison pill? It ended September with $29.6 billion in debt and finance leases (without operating leases and pension obligations). The “100% approved” isn’t at all credible, unless he means only at the federal level and because he’s had assurances from the President (who could change his mind!). It has been revealed that those points transfer to a variety of airline and hotel programs, now even including American AAdvantage. By the way, this card earns AAdvantage miles faster than the American Airlines cards to (even unbonused spend with this card earns 1.5x, versus just 1 mile per dollar with American Airlines cobrands).

Many of the card’s annual benefits are on a calendar year basis so you have the opportunity to take advantage of them twice in your first cardmember year: the $300 hotel benefit for 2+ night stays booked through Citi Travel; the $200 Splurge credit (take it for American Airlines travel!), and $100 in Blacklane credits twice each year. That’s $1,200 in credits you can reap in year 1 if you’re approved now. Ken Paxton Spotted Fleeing Texas With Girlfriend After Voters Reject His Senate Bid—Flying Coach To Fiji

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read | Source: Viewfromthewing

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Senate race, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton was photographed at San Francisco airport with his girlfriend, Tracy Duhon, wearing a straw hat and carrying a Republican Attorneys General Association backpack.
  • According to recent reports, they departed Wednesday night, November 11.
  • Michael Board shares the photo of Ken Paxton and Tracy Duhon at San Francisco airport.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Eight days after losing his U.S. Senate race, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton was photographed at San Francisco airport with his girlfriend, Tracy Duhon, wearing a straw hat and carrying a Republican Attorneys General Association backpack. They were apparently headed to Fiji. And photos show them in coach. They departed Wednesday night, November 11. A witness says they worried about their bags making it to Fiji. Michael Board shares the photo of Ken Paxton and Tracy Duhon at San Francisco airport Another photo reveals them standing in the aisle of coach. TMZ: Ken Paxton spotted in San Francisco International Airport, witness says he was traveling to Fiji https://t.co/GNFXuDuPvY — Kalshi Politics (@KalshiPolitics) November 12, 2026 Meanwhile, Paxton’s divorce finalized Thursday. State Senator Angela Paxton filed to end their 38-year marriage last year “on biblical grounds.” I’ve covered the travels of Ted Cruz, Elizabeth Warren, AOC, Bernie Sanders and others, and the credit card spend habits of former Wisconsin Governor Scott Walker. This choice isn’t partisan. Paxton Has A History Of Getting Out Of Town A Texas politician fleeing the state for warmer climes brings to mind Ted Cruz flying to Cancún during the February 2021 winter storm while millions of Texans were without power. This time the disaster was electoral. But Paxton has his own winter storm escape story. He and his then-wife went to Utah during that same freeze, saying he had meetings with Utah’s attorney general about the state Google antitrust case. This summer, I wrote about Paxton spending America’s 250th birthday in London with Duhon. He marked the anniversary of separating from Britain by going to Britain. The pair had been spotted traveling through Washington Dulles on their way to Iceland in late June. Then came the London video, with Marriott County Hall in the background. They apparently flew economy on that trip. Video of Ken Paxton and Tracy Duhon in London over the Fourth of July weekend In October, the Wall Street Journal reported on video of Paxton and Duhon celebrating Latest Year’s Eve 2024 overlooking the Burj Khalifa fireworks with fugitives indicted in a federal healthcare fraud case who had contributed $190,000 to Paxton’s campaign. James Talarico’s campaign shares footage of Ken Paxton at the Dubai gathering Republicans Knew Who They Were Nominating The Republican-controlled Texas House impeached Attorney General Paxton. Paxton’s own senior staff reported him to the FBI. House investigators alleged that an Austin real estate developer provided home renovations and helped conceal Paxton’s activities, including through an Uber account under the name “Dave P.” He also employed a woman Paxton previously had an affair with. The Uber account apparently let Paxton carry on his affair and visit his donor without his security detail or using his identifiable state vehicle. In return, Paxton allegedly used his office to help the developer. One example was a rushed legal opinion invoking pandemic restrictions to stop foreclosure auctions. The Texas Senate, under pressure large donors and the Lieutenant Governor, acquitted him in 2023. He’d also spent years under state felony securities fraud charges. That case ended through an agreement requiring restitution, community service and ethics training. The federal corruption investigation ended without charges. President Trump endorsed Paxton against incumbent Senator John Cornyn a week before their May runoff. Republicans then had to spend heavily defending a seat they’d held for decades, with a candidate that may have been one of the worst campaigners I’ve seen in 30 years even apart from his past challenges. Here he is wearing a reported-$40,000 watch and a Four Seasons golf shirt. And this clip of him was promoted by his campaign: .@KenPaxtonTX: The future of our state and the future of our country ride on this race. https://t.co/2ZvVWdhwzp — Paxton War Room (@PaxtonsPatriots) August 29, 2026 That choice cost Republicans dearly. Cornyn would’ve been far better-positioned in the general election. Counterfactuals are hard, but the rest of his party’s nominees at the state level were clearly brought down by his place on the ticket. Republicans even appeared in advertising against him. Former Republican state Representative Glenn Rogers, who’d voted to impeach Paxton, appeared in a pro-Talarico ad saying he’d never trust or support Paxton. The most revealing ad may have been the one Angela Paxton made because polls demonstrated over 10% of Republicans staying home. While divorcing him, she urged Republicans to vote without mentioning her husband by name: “It’s about getting the whole team across the finish line.” Paxton wasn’t the only Republican with problems. Governor Greg Abbott had helped defeat Republican legislators who opposed school choice in the 2024 primaries. That left resentment in rural communities where public schools are major employers, and there are fewer private school options where the vouchers could be used. Republicans also faced a terrible national election environment, with an unpopular President and high gas prices. I Even Agree With Him On Some Of His Lawsuits Just this morning, I wrote about Austin’s airport rail plans and the financing arrangement Paxton’s office challenged. The city raised property taxes, then routed the money through a separate corporation to matter the debt, allowing the city to claim that it isn’t borrowing. Economically, property taxes support the bonds, while the city claims its not running afoul on state borrowing rules. The arrangement is probably illegal, but the state’s new attorney general may not be as inclined to continue the litigation. Credit: Gage Skidmore via Wikimedia Commons Even where they might agree with Paxton on an issue, plenty of Texans would’ve been happy for him to leave much earlier, even without a ticket to Fiji.
